pr.title: Draw a drawer's labels as colored text, lightened or darkened to read on the panel
pr.head: 8ecebf2777fad7349443205fd2222517f1fbc035

summary: Projector's Claude Code mod draws a panel above the prompt that lists the session's pull requests. Opening a pull request's drawer shows a line of facts about it: the session's roles, the branch, the diff size, the checks, and last the pull request's GitHub labels. Until this change each label was a pill: its name padded with spaces on a fill of the label's GitHub color, in black or white text. In a terminal those blocks of color are loud next to the rest of the line, which is plain colored text separated by ·.

This change draws each label like the other facts: its name in the label's own color, with no fill, set off by · . A bare color must now read against the panel's own background, and some GitHub colors do not, such as dark red #b60205 on the dark theme or pale yellow #fbca04 on the light theme. So the new labelColor function measures each label's WCAG contrast ratio against the background and, below 3:1, mixes it toward white or black in steps of a twentieth until it reaches 3:1.
Only the drawing changes. The label names that GitHub stores, and the reviewing and clean labels that decide a row's state word, are read exactly as before.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Drawer: the lines that open under a pull request's row in the panel when you press its number.
  • Contrast ratio: WCAG's measure of how far apart two colors' luminances are, from 1:1 (identical) to 21:1 (black on white). 3:1 is WCAG's minimum for large text.
  • Panel background: rgb(20,20,20) on the dark themes, rgb(240,240,240) on the light ones, inverseText on an ANSI theme, or whatever panel.background sets.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One open finding: the example panel in docs/plugins.md still shows the old two-space gap before a label.
  • The gate passed on this head: 236 hook tests, the type check, and the plugin validations, and CI's check job.

groups.title: Labels drawn as colored text
groups.kicker: How the drawer picks each label's color and lays the labels out
intro: hooks/register.tsx holds the whole mod. The change replaces labelStyle, which returned a fill and a black or white text color, with labelColor, which returns one text color for the label's name on the panel's background.

labelColor parses both colors with rgbOf, computes WCAG relative luminance with luminanceOf, and compares them with contrastOf. A label that already reaches 3:1 keeps its own color. Otherwise it is mixed toward white when white contrasts more with the background, or toward black when black does, one twentieth at a time, and the first mix that reaches 3:1 is drawn. A background with no color the panel can measure, such as inverseText, ansi256(n), or the sidebar setting, counts as black, so the panel only ever lightens a too-dark label there.

checks.text: The panel reads 3:1 rather than WCAG's 4.5:1 for text this size on purpose: 4.5:1 would shift GitHub's common green #0e8a16 and purple #7057ff away from the colors people recognize. Both already clear 3:1 on both themes.

files.note: Adds labelColor and its color helpers, and draws each label in the drawer's facts line as bare colored text.

checks.text: Worked by hand: #b60205 has a luminance of about 0.0999, a 2.999:1 contrast with black, so one step toward white gives #ba0f12, the value the light-ansi test expects. Full white or full black always clears 3:1 against any background, so the loop returns before its fallback.

color here is the panel's background, read from panel.background or the theme a few hundred lines up. A label with no color yet, which an old daemon cache leaves, is a plain string in the default text color.

files.note: Turns the single label test into one case per theme, dark, light, and light-ansi, and adds a dark red breaking label to the fixture.

checks.text: Each case compares every label's text and computed color with literal values, so a wrong name, a raw unadjusted color, or a color on the colorless legacy label turns it red. All 236 hook tests passed on this head.
